# Catalog purpose

The catalog distinguishes:

- implemented pipelines;
- active development work;
- planned components;
- components requiring scientific review;
- components not yet formally assessed.

A component’s presence in the catalog does not mean that its pipeline has already been validated.

# Status definitions

```{=html}
<div class="status-grid">

  <div class="status-card">
    <span class="status-badge status-validated">
      Validated
    </span>
    <h3>Release-ready</h3>
    <p>
      Implemented, tested, documented, and included in a formal release.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="status-card">
    <span class="status-badge status-development">
      In development
    </span>
    <h3>Actively being built</h3>
    <p>
      Coding, validation, scientific review, or documentation is underway.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="status-card">
    <span class="status-badge status-planned">
      Planned
    </span>
    <h3>Accepted into the roadmap</h3>
    <p>
      Included in future development plans but not yet implemented.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="status-card">
    <span class="status-badge status-research">
      Research required
    </span>
    <h3>Scientific review needed</h3>
    <p>
      Eligibility, methods, weights, record structure, or harmonization require further investigation.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="status-card">
    <span class="status-badge status-unassessed">
      Not yet assessed
    </span>
    <h3>Scope not yet reviewed</h3>
    <p>
      The component has not undergone formal technical or scientific assessment.
    </p>
  </div>

</div>
```

<script>
(function () {
  const buttons =
    document.querySelectorAll(
      ".catalog-filter-button"
    );

  const cards =
    document.querySelectorAll(
      ".component-card"
    );

  buttons.forEach(
    function (button) {
      button.addEventListener(
        "click",
        function () {
          const selectedFilter =
            button.getAttribute(
              "data-filter"
            );

          buttons.forEach(
            function (item) {
              item.classList.remove(
                "active"
              );
            }
          );

          button.classList.add(
            "active"
          );

          cards.forEach(
            function (card) {
              const status =
                card.getAttribute(
                  "data-status"
                );

              const showCard =
                selectedFilter === "all" ||
                status === selectedFilter;

              card.hidden =
                !showCard;
            }
          );
        }
      );
    }
  );
})();
</script>

# Component onboarding pathway

Every new component should pass through four broad stages.

```{=html}
<div class="onboarding-path">

  <div class="onboarding-step">
    <div class="onboarding-step-number">1</div>
    <strong>Scope</strong>
    <span>
      Define the component, cycles, research purpose, and analytical population.
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="onboarding-step">
    <div class="onboarding-step-number">2</div>
    <strong>Scientific review</strong>
    <span>
      Assess eligibility, methods, units, record structure, and weights.
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="onboarding-step">
    <div class="onboarding-step-number">3</div>
    <strong>Implementation</strong>
    <span>
      Build manifests, crosswalks, scripts, validation rules, and outputs.
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="onboarding-step">
    <div class="onboarding-step-number">4</div>
    <strong>Release</strong>
    <span>
      Test, document, review, publish, and assign validated status.
    </span>
  </div>

</div>
```

# Component onboarding requirements

```{=html}
<div class="requirement-grid">

  <div class="requirement-card">

      <li><code>survey_cycle</code></li>
      <li><code>file_name</code></li>
      <li><code>source_url</code></li>
      <li><code>record_level</code></li>

      <li><code>analytic_role</code></li>

  </div>

  <div class="requirement-card">
    <h3>2. Variable crosswalk</h3>
    <p>Minimum fields:</p>
    <ul>
      <li><code>survey_cycle</code></li>
      <li><code>source_variable</code></li>
      <li><code>harmonized_variable</code></li>
      <li><code>label</code></li>
      <li><code>unit</code></li>
      <li><code>method</code></li>
      <li><code>decision</code></li>
      <li><code>notes</code></li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="requirement-card">
    <h3>3. Eligibility review</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>eligible ages;</li>
      <li>sex restrictions;</li>
      <li>pregnancy restrictions;</li>
      <li>examination requirements;</li>
      <li>fasting requirements;</li>
      <li>subsample selection;</li>
      <li>collection-session restrictions.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="requirement-card">
    <h3>4. Laboratory-method review</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>specimen type;</li>
      <li>instrument;</li>
      <li>method;</li>
      <li>laboratory;</li>
      <li>detection limits;</li>
      <li>quality-control notes;</li>
      <li>corrections;</li>
      <li>comparability decisions.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="requirement-card">
    <h3>5. Weight guidance</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>candidate interview or MEC weight;</li>
      <li>specialized subsample weight;</li>
      <li>multi-cycle construction;</li>
      <li>exclusions;</li>
      <li>limitations.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="requirement-card">
    <h3>6. Record-level contract</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>one record per participant;</li>
      <li>multiple records per participant;</li>
      <li>repeat examinations;</li>
      <li>replicate measurements;</li>
      <li>specimen-level records.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="requirement-card">
    <h3>7. Validation rules</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>source-file existence;</li>
      <li>HTTP success;</li>
      <li>expected variables;</li>
      <li>expected key;</li>
      <li>key uniqueness where required;</li>
      <li>cycle consistency;</li>
      <li>row-count review;</li>
      <li>missingness review;</li>
      <li>join-contract testing.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="requirement-card">
    <h3>8. Required outputs</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>processed RDS;</li>
      <li>optional CSV;</li>
      <li>provenance manifest;</li>
      <li>validation summary;</li>
      <li>duplicate report;</li>
      <li>unresolved-conflict report;</li>
      <li>package-version record;</li>
      <li>session information.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

</div>
```

# How development priorities are selected

```{=html}
<div class="priority-grid">

  <div class="priority-card">
    <strong>Public-health relevance</strong>
    <span>
      Does the component support important clinical, epidemiological, or policy questions?
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="priority-card">
    <strong>Cycle availability</strong>
    <span>
      Is the component available across enough cycles to support useful analysis?
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="priority-card">
    <strong>Methodological complexity</strong>
    <span>
      Are methods, eligibility, weights, and harmonization manageable?
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="priority-card">
    <strong>Learner demand</strong>
    <span>
      Is there clear educational or analytical interest in the component?
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="priority-card">
    <strong>Architectural fit</strong>
    <span>
      Can the component use or extend the current pipeline structure?
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="priority-card">
    <strong>Documentation quality</strong>
    <span>
      Are official files, methods, eligibility notes, and weight guidance available?
    </span>
  </div>

  <div class="priority-card">
    <strong>Scientific collaboration</strong>
    <span>
      Is suitable subject-matter expertise available for review?
    </span>
  </div>

</div>
```

# Requesting a component

Before proposing a new laboratory pipeline, identify:

- the desired laboratory component;
- the survey cycles;
- the primary research question;
- required supporting variables;
- the intended population;
- whether weighted national inference is required.

Requests may be submitted through the project’s GitHub issue tracker.

# Catalog limitations

::: {.callout-warning icon="true"}
## This catalog is a roadmap, not an analytical authorization

It does not replace:

- official NHANES component documentation;
- laboratory methods documentation;
- analytical guidelines;
- current release notes;
- cycle-specific scientific review;
- expert judgment.
:::

# Page summary

A component becomes a validated pipeline only after it has passed through:

```text
scope definition
scientific review
source mapping
variable harmonization
weight selection
record-level validation
reproducibility testing
documentation
release review
```

The catalog therefore distinguishes between:

```text
interest
planning
research
implementation
validation
```

That distinction protects users from treating an analytical roadmap as a finished scientific product.
